turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Hale. I have a client call at 4:40, so you have twenty minutes. Owen saw a zero on his phone in the middle of class and nobody called me, so who decided that, and on what basis?
The checker said 94 percent. That's the end of it.

"The end of it." Turnitin's own guide says that number "should not be used as the sole basis for adverse actions against a student," and your school's procedure 4.3 says software alone doesn't establish anything. So withdraw the zero, or tell me what else you have before I walk upstairs to the principal.
I don't need more proof than that.

I'm writing that down: "I don't need more proof than that." Your own procedure says you speak to Owen first and call me before any mark goes in, and you did neither. Withdraw the zero today, or I'm in the principal's office at 4:40 instead of on my call.
The software doesn't lie, unlike some people.

"Unlike some people." Say his name, Hale, if you're calling my son a liar, and then tell me whether you're calling me one too. My son doesn't lie, and this meeting is going to the principal and then to the board under section 42.

Then I want it in writing tonight: who decided, on what basis besides a machine's number, and whether anything is on Owen's record right now. That zero is costing him up to ten and a half points on his final mark with a scholarship deadline on December 1, and I won't let this school do to him what it did to his sister. Answer the record question now, Hale, because the principal's office is my next stop.
